title: Wichita State University football team plane crash
summary: A Martin 404 carrying the Wichita State University football team crashed into Mount Trelease near Loveland Pass, Colorado. The aircraft attempted a scenic route through a mountain valley without adequate flight planning. The overloaded aircraft became trapped in a box canyon unable to climb over surrounding ridges, struck trees, and was destroyed by impact and fire.
probable_cause: The probable cause of this accident was the intentional operation of the aircraft over a mountain valley route at an altitude from which the aircraft could neither climb over the obstructing terrain ahead, nor execute a successful course reversal. Significant factors were the overloaded condition of the aircraft, the virtual absence of flight planning for the chosen route, a lack of understanding of aircraft performance capabilities and limitations, and the lack of operational management to monitor and appropriately control the actions of the flightcrew. (p. 31-32)

factors.evidence: Flight crew departed from planned route via established airways and instead proceeded on scenic route through Clear Creek Valley without adequate flight planning (p. 31-32).
Aircraft was 5,190 pounds over maximum takeoff weight at Denver and 2,665 pounds over maximum takeoff weight at impact (p. 32).
Aircraft became trapped in box canyon at Dry Gulch unable to climb over surrounding ridges or execute successful reversal turn (p. 31-32).
Aircraft struck trees at 10,800 feet elevation on Mount Trelease, descended 425 feet through trees while spinning (p. 2).
Aircraft was destroyed by fire and impact after striking trees (p. 2).

events.text: First Officer Skipper purchases aeronautical sectional charts at Denver for scenic route (p. 4)
Aircraft departs Denver Stapleton, N464M takes off on scenic route through Clear Creek Valley (p. 4-5)
Aircraft passes Georgetown at approximately 9,800 feet msl (p. 25-26)
Aircraft flying low through Clear Creek Valley, all witnesses report altitude below mountaintops (p. 7)
First Officer Skipper tells captain they should reverse course and gain altitude at Dry Gulch (p. 5)
First Officer Skipper initiates right turn, then Captain Crocker takes control (p. 5)
Captain Crocker executes steep left turn attempting to avoid rising terrain (p. 5)
Aircraft strikes trees at 10,800 feet on east slope of Mount Trelease (p. 2)
Aircraft continues 425 feet through trees at 215° heading, destroyed by fire and impact (p. 2)
